Rashi on Nedarim 21b:1:1.hebrew: מי דמי גבי צונן צדיקים אומרים מעט ועושין הרבה - וזה שהיה מסרב בחבירו שיאכל אצלו קימעא וישתה טיפת צונן, ודאי לאכילה ושתיה מרובה קאמר, כי כן דרכן של צדיקים לומר מעט ולעשות הרבה. וכי אמר ליה האי: "קונם טיפת צונן שאני טועם", הכי נתכוון לומר: אותה טיפה שאתה רוצה ליתן לי איני טועם — דהיינו אכילה מרובה — ולא נתכוון לטיפת צונן ממש. הלכך, אסור באכילה ושתיה מרובה, ומותר לשתות הימנו טיפת צונן. אבל הכא, דדילמא האי דאמר טפי מסלע דעתיה על פחות מסלע ליתן בשלשה דינרין, והאי דאמר בציר דעתיה על יותר משקל ליתן ג' דינרין:
Rashi on Nedarim 21b:1:1.english: Are [they] comparable? Concerning cold [water], the righteous say little and do much - And this [host] who was urging his fellow to eat a little with him and drink a drop of cold [water] certainly meant a large [amount of] food and drink, for such is the way of the righteous: to say little and do much. And when this [guest] said to him, "Konam [any] drop of cold [water] that I taste," this is what he intended to say: "That 'drop' that you wish to give me I will not taste" — which means a large [amount of] food — and he did not intend an actual drop of cold [water]. Therefore, he is forbidden from [having] a large [amount of] food and drink, and he is permitted to drink a drop of cold [water] from him. But here, [it is not comparable,] for perhaps this one who said "more than a sela" had in mind less than a sela, to give [it] for three dinars, and this one who said "less [than a shekel]" had in mind more than a shekel, to give three dinars.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:2:1.english: And it is [a vow of] exhortation - And it is permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:2:2.english: Or perhaps he meant [it] specifically, and it is a vow - and [it is] forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:4:1.hebrew: אלא כעין ד' נדרים [הללו] - והני הוא דשרו משום דלית בהו ממש, אבל שאר נדרים אין אדם רשאי להתיר עד שיתחרט הנודר מעצמו:
Rashi on Nedarim 21b:4:1.english: Only similar to these four vows - And it is these that are permitted [to be dissolved] because there is no substance in them, but [as for] other vows, a person is not permitted to dissolve [them] until the one who vowed regrets [it] on his own.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:4:2.hebrew: קסבר אין פותחין בחרטה - שאין חכם רשאי לפתוח ולומד לו: "נדרת אדעתא דהכי?", כדאמרינן לקמן; אלא הנודר הוא יתחרט תחלה, ויפתח ויאמר לו: "לא לדעת כן נדרתי", והוא פותח תחלה בחרטה:
Rashi on Nedarim 21b:4:2.english: He holds [that] we do not open with regret - For a sage is not permitted to open and say to him, "Did you vow with this in mind?", as we say later; rather, the one who vowed must regret [it] first, and open and say to him, "I did not vow with that in mind," and [thus] he opens first with regret.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:5:1.english: [He] said to him: Is your heart upon you? - That is to say, do you stand by [your] original mind, that your desire is still for that vow?

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:5:2.hebrew: אמר ליה לא - כלומר מתחרט אכי, אלמא קסבר פותחין בחרטה:
Rashi on Nedarim 21b:5:2.english: He said to him: No - That is to say, I regret [it]; thus, he holds [that] we broach [dissolution] based on regret.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:6:1.hebrew: אם היו י' בני אדם כו' - שאם פתחו לך בחרטה כשרצית לנדור, כלום נדרת:
Rashi on Nedarim 21b:6:1.english: Had there been ten people, etc. - [That is,] if they had opened [an avenue of] regret for you when you wanted to vow, would you have vowed at all?

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:6:2.hebrew: אמר ליה לאו - קסבר אין פותחין בחרטה, ולכך אמר ליה כה"ג, דכיון דאמר: אילו היו י' בני אדם כו', דמיעקר עקר לנדריה ולא הוי נדר כלל, ולכך פותח בחרטה הוא, אבל בעלמא אין פותחין בחרטה:
Rashi on Nedarim 21b:6:2.english: He said to him: No - He holds [that] we do not open [a vow] with regret, and therefore he said to him in this manner; for since he said, "Had there been ten people, etc.," he completely uproots his vow and it is not a vow at all, and therefore he opens with regret [in this case], whereas in general we do not open [a vow] with regret.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:7:1.hebrew: קסבר רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, אין פותחין בחרטה:
Rashi on Nedarim 21b:7:1.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, holds [that] one does not open [a vow] with regret.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:9:2.hebrew: כדו תהית - מצטער אתה שנדרת? דהיינו בחרטה:
Rashi on Nedarim 21b:9:2.english: Do you now regret - Are you regretful that you vowed? That is, [dissolution] through regret.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:9:3.english: Did you want to vow? - Did you accept the vow willingly?

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:9:4.english: If they had not angered me - Had they not angered me, I would not have vowed.

Rashi on Nedarim 21b:9:5.hebrew: דאמרן מגירתיך - שאומרות השכינות על בתך, כמו ומגרת ביתה (שמות ג):
Rashi on Nedarim 21b:9:5.english: That your neighbors [megirateikh] would say - That the neighbors say about your daughter, like "and of the dweller in her house [u'megarat beitah]" (Exodus 3).

Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:4:1.hebrew: ורב יוסף נמי מתני לקולא - אפילו לרב אסי כדאמר, דהלכתא דד' נדרים אין צריכין שאלה, דבשל סופרים הלך אחר המיקל. וכן פסק הר"ר אליעזר ממי"ץ בשם רבי יעקב:
Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:4:1.english: And Rav Yosef also teaches [it] leniently - even according to Rav Asi, as he states, [so] that the halakha is that [the] four vows do not require a request [to a halakhic authority], for in [matters] of rabbinic [law] one follows the lenient [opinion]. And so ruled Rabbi Eliezer of Metz in the name of Rabbi Yaakov.

Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:4:2.hebrew: אלא כעין ארבעה נדרים - שפותחין ואומרין: "(לאו) אדעתא דהכי מי נדרת?", והוא אומר לא נתכוון לנדור — אלא כעין ד' נדרים שלא נתכוון בהם לאיסור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:4:2.english: Only like [these] four vows - For they broach [the vow] and say: "([Is it] not) with this in mind that you vowed?" and he says [that] he did not intend to vow — rather, [it is] like the four vows in which he did not intend [to create] a prohibition.

Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:4:3.hebrew: קסבר אין פותחין לנודר בחרטה - לומר לו: "מתחרט אתה, שהיית רוצה שלא יהיה עליך נדר מתחלה?", דההוא פתח לא משוי ליה בהדיא נדר טעות; אלא אומר לו: "אדעתא דהכי נדרת?", והוא אומר: "אילו ידעתי כן, לא הייתי נודר", דמשוי ליה נדר טעות מעיקרא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:4:3.english: He holds that one does not broach [dissolution] for one who vows based on regret - [That is,] to say to him, "Do you regret [it], such that you would wish that there had not been a vow upon you from the beginning?" For that opening does not explicitly render it a vow [made] in error. Rather, he says to him, "Did you vow with this in mind?" and he says, "Had I known this, I would not have vowed," which renders it a vow [made] in error from the outset.

Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:5:1.hebrew: אמר ליה לבך עלך - פי': לבך שהיה עליך בשעת נדר, יש בו עליך עדיין, ואין אתה מתחרט מעיקרא אלא מכאן ולהבא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:5:1.english: He said to him: "Is your heart upon you?" - Explanation: Your heart [i.e., mindset] that was upon you at the time of the vow — is it still upon you? And you do not regret [the vow] from the outset, but rather from now and onward.

Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:5:2.hebrew: אמר ליה לא - אלא מתחרט אני על שנדרתי כל עיקר. ודוקא כשמתחרט מעיקרא, כדפרישית; אבל אם אינו מתחרט מעיקרא אלא מכאן ולהבא, לכ"ע אין פותחין בחרטה זו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:5:2.english: He said to him: No - rather, I regret having vowed altogether. And [this applies] specifically when he regrets [it] from the outset, as I explained [earlier]; but if he does not regret [it] from the outset, [and regrets it] only from now on, according to all opinions one does not broach [dissolution] with this regret.

Tosafot on Nedarim 21b:5:3.english: And he dissolved [the vow] for him - For he holds [that] one may broach [dissolution] based on regret.
